findings.title: Role, ownership and default-privilege facts; no RLS or tenant context yet; app role can set arbitrary GUCs
evidence: deploy/postgres/init/01-roles.sh:16-21 gozleme_migrator NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS owns database; gozleme_app NOSUPERUSER NOCREATEDB NOCREATEROLE NOBYPASSRLS NOINHERIT

src/Gozleme.Api/Persistence/Migrations/20261114000000_Foundation.cs:18-24 creates schema gozleme and ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES granting SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE on all future tables to gozleme_app
Live stack: pg_default_acl shows gozleme_app=arwd/gozleme_migrator and rU on sequences; schema gozleme owned by gozleme_migrator
Live stack (rolled-back transaction): SET ROLE gozleme_app; SET LOCAL app.tenant_id = 'x' succeeds
No RLS policy, tenant column or tenant-context code exists at e7904ad
findings.recommendation: Tenant-owned tables enable RLS and policies in the same migration that creates them; GOZ-0003 decides FORCE RLS explicitly (migrator owns all tables), adds a catalog test for relrowsecurity, retrofits GOZ-0001/0002 tables, and treats the tenant GUC as defence in depth only.

findings.title: Default privileges grant UPDATE/DELETE on every future table, including those that must be immutable or append-only
evidence: src/Gozleme.Api/Persistence/Migrations/20261114000000_Foundation.cs:21
docs/architecture/security-invariants.md invariant 6 (immutable signed publications)
findings.recommendation: Creating migrations for immutable/append-only tables REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE from gozleme_app (or enforce equivalently) and prove database-level rejection with an integration test as gozleme_app.

findings.title: pgvector cannot be created by the migrator role; pg_trgm can
evidence: Live stack: /usr/share/postgresql/17/extension/vector.control (default_version 0.8.6) has no 'trusted = true'
Live stack (rolled-back transaction): SET ROLE gozleme_migrator; CREATE EXTENSION vector -> ERROR permission denied to create extension "vector", HINT Must be superuser
Live stack (rolled-back transaction): SET ROLE gozleme_migrator; CREATE EXTENSION pg_trgm SCHEMA gozleme succeeds (pg_trgm.control trusted = true)
src/Gozleme.Api/Status/DatabaseProbe.cs:22-27 vector.available = pg_available_extensions, vector.enabled = pg_extension
tests/Gozleme.Api.IntegrationTests/OptionalVectorTests.cs proves health on postgres:17-alpine
findings.recommendation: GOZ-0015 provides an operator/superuser provisioning step for vector (opt-in Compose init script, Helm prerequisite), keeps vector objects conditional, and exposes semantic-search state separately from vector.enabled via contract revision. Granting superuser to either application role requires human approval and is not recommended.

src/Gozleme.Api/Status/StatusService.cs:24-25 degraded only when a required dependency is unhealthy
web/src/lib/status.ts:42-74 strict structural validation; unknown shapes become invalid-response
Re-analysis at 930128e: prompt text for 0009/0010/0011/0015/0016 updated to reflect the corrected validator tolerance

findings.title: Web status validator is stricter than the OpenAPI contract for capabilities
evidence: docs/specs/000-repository-bootstrap/contracts/status-api.openapi.yaml: capabilities is object|null with optional property vector (no required list)
web/src/lib/status.ts:44-50 rejects any non-null capabilities lacking a valid vector object, so a contract-valid {} renders as invalid-response/unreachable

Re-analysis at 930128e: web/src/lib/status.ts isDependency now accepts capabilities null or an object whose vector is absent or a valid {available,enabled}; status.test.ts adds 'accepts capabilities without the optional vector entry' and a malformed-vector rejection case; StatusDashboard.tsx:56 already uses optional chaining; typecheck and 18 Vitest tests pass at HEAD
findings.recommendation: Corrective change in GOZ-0000: either mark vector required inside capabilities in the OpenAPI, or relax isDependency to accept capabilities objects where vector is absent or valid; add a Vitest case for the chosen rule.

.gitignore:33-34 ignores __pycache__/ and *.pyc

findings.title: No JavaScript dependency vulnerability check in CI
evidence: docs/engineering/ci-quality-gates.md requires 'code secret scanning and dependency checks'
.github/workflows/ci.yml has gitleaks but no pnpm audit or dependency-review step; .NET relies on SDK-default NuGet audit plus TreatWarningsAsErrors (Directory.Build.props), not explicitly configured

Re-analysis at 930128e: ci.yml frontend job runs 'pnpm audit --prod --audit-level low'; Directory.Build.props sets NuGetAudit true, NuGetAuditMode all, NuGetAuditLevel low and NU1901-NU1904 as errors. Downstream note: any spec adding a NuGet or production npm package now fails CI on any published advisory, including low severity; future specs must resolve or explicitly and documentedly suppress, never silently disable the audit
findings.recommendation: Add a pnpm audit (or dependency-review) step and set NuGetAudit/NuGetAuditMode explicitly; non-blocking for FR-015, which does not list dependency checks.

findings.title: Unauthenticated browser telemetry ingestion route
evidence: web/src/app/api/otel/v1/traces/route.ts:1-36 accepts any JSON/protobuf POST up to 256 KiB and forwards it to the collector; no authentication, origin check or rate limit (comment: unauthenticated until GOZ-0001)
Browser-supplied resource attributes (e.g. service.name) are forwarded unmodified, so a caller can inject spans claiming to be gozleme-api or gozleme-web into the trace store
In Helm the web tier is the public front end, so the route is reachable by any client
findings.recommendation: GOZ-0001 decides and implements authentication or session binding, origin checking and rate limiting for the route. Consider pinning or overwriting service.name for the browser pipeline at the collector, so browser data cannot impersonate server services. GOZ-0039 verifies this as a release gate.

findings.title: Telemetry is sensitive, cross-tenant, operator-visible data
evidence: Live Jaeger (/api/v3/traces, service gozleme-api) shows span attributes db.query.text (full SQL text), http.url, http.target, url.path, user_agent.original
deploy/otel/collector.yaml redaction matches credential-like keys and values only (password, token, api key, connection string, host/username patterns); it cannot recognise tenant-private metadata
docs/architecture/security-invariants.md invariant 8 names traces explicitly; invariant 3 (no existence leaks); decision R3-19 (operator vs tenant support access)
findings.recommendation: Keep confidential values out of span names, attributes, metric labels, SQL text and URLs (parameters only; no private search terms in query strings). GOZ-0003 decides whether an opaque tenant ID may appear as an attribute. Collector redaction stays defence in depth.

findings.title: Stored and searchable logs and telemetry retention are undecided
evidence: deploy/otel/collector.yaml logs pipeline exports only to the debug (console) exporter
compose.yaml jaeger service uses default in-memory storage, so traces are lost on restart; Prometheus is only a scrape endpoint (:8889), with no storage
docs/engineering/local-development.md:15 logs via make logs and docker compose logs otel-collector
findings.recommendation: Human decides whether Gözleme ships durable, searchable log, trace or metric storage (local and Helm) and its retention and erasure policy, which interacts with CR-07 deletion and with audit receipts. Until then, prompts carry no storage or retention requirement.

findings.title: Collector configuration is not hot-reloaded and Helm ships no collector
evidence: compose.yaml otel-collector mounts deploy/otel/collector.yaml read-only; changes take effect only after a restart
docs/engineering/local-development.md:37-38 already documents running docker compose restart otel-collector
deploy/helm/gozleme: telemetry.* only points at an operator-provided OTLP endpoint; the redaction processors exist only in the local collector config
findings.recommendation: No prompt change needed for the reload caveat, which is documented. For Helm, document in the chart README that operators must apply equivalent redaction in their own collector, since the app-side no-secret rules are the primary control. GOZ-0039 covers this through its Helm telemetry gate.

findings.title: Browser ingestion route drops any path prefix of the OTLP endpoint
evidence: web/src/app/api/otel/v1/traces/route.ts:26 new URL("/v1/traces", endpoint) resolves an absolute path, so an endpoint such as https://otel.example/otlp is forwarded to https://otel.example/v1/traces
The OTLP/HTTP exporter convention appends v1/traces to the configured base endpoint path; the server-side @vercel/otel exporter uses the same variable
findings.recommendation: Corrective change in GOZ-0000: append the signal path to the endpoint (trim the trailing slash, then add /v1/traces) and add a unit test with a path-prefixed endpoint.
